## What This Code Does

This demo generates a population of agents using the model's initialization routines and analyses the statistical properties of key attributes — resilience, affect, resources, and PSS-10. It computes descriptive statistics (mean, SD, skewness, kurtosis, CV, IQR), checks bounds enforcement, measures population diversity, validates reproducibility across runs, and tests edge case robustness.

## Helper: Mock Model

::: {#mock .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
class MockModel:
    def __init__(self, seed=None):
        self.seed = seed
        self.agents = []
        self.register_agent = lambda x: None
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
```
:::


## Generate Population

::: {#generate .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
demo_config = {
    "initial_resilience_mean": 0.6, "initial_resilience_sd": 0.15,
    "initial_affect_mean": 0.1, "initial_affect_sd": 0.25,
    "initial_resources_mean": 0.7, "initial_resources_sd": 0.12,
    "stress_probability": 0.5, "coping_success_rate": 0.5, "subevents_per_day": 3,
}

agents = []
for i in range(500):
    model = MockModel(seed=1000 + i)
    agent = Person(model, demo_config)
    agents.append(agent)

resilience = np.array([a.resilience for a in agents])
affect = np.array([a.affect for a in agents])
resources = np.array([a.resources for a in agents])
pss10 = np.array([a.pss10 for a in agents])
```
:::


## Population Statistics

::: {#stats .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def describe(values, name):
    print(f"\n{name}:")
    print(f"  Mean: {np.mean(values):.3f}  SD: {np.std(values, ddof=1):.3f}")
    print(f"  Range: [{np.min(values):.3f}, {np.max(values):.3f}]")
    print(f"  Median: {np.median(values):.3f}  IQR: {np.percentile(values, 75) - np.percentile(values, 25):.3f}")
    print(f"  Skewness: {pd.Series(values).skew():.3f}  Kurtosis: {pd.Series(values).kurtosis():.3f}")

describe(resilience, "Resilience")
describe(affect, "Affect")
describe(resources, "Resources")
describe(pss10, "PSS-10")
```

## Bounds Checks

::: {#bounds .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
all_in_bounds = all(0 <= a.resilience <= 1 and -1 <= a.affect <= 1 and 0 <= a.resources <= 1 for a in agents)
print(f"All agents within valid bounds: {all_in_bounds}")

unique_res = len(set(np.round(resilience, 3)))
unique_aff = len(set(np.round(affect, 3)))
print(f"Unique resilience values: {unique_res}  Unique affect values: {unique_aff}")
```

## Why This Matters for the Simulation

Population variation analysis ensures that the agent initialization produces realistic diversity. If all agents were nearly identical, the simulation would lack emergent complexity. The skewness and kurtosis diagnostics reveal whether attribute distributions match real-world patterns, and bounds enforcement guarantees numerical stability throughout the simulation lifecycle.
